drills.title: Sharks and Fishes
drills.objective: Change direction into space.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Runners cross between end lines; one or two sharks tag them. Tagged runners become sharks next round. Reset until all have crossed.
drills.coaching: Look up; change pace; avoid bunching.
drills.regression: Widen area or use one shark.
drills.progression: Carry a ball in two hands.
drills.questions: Where was the gap before you started? What changed when the shark moved?
drills.notes: Watch whether the quieter runners reach the line as often as the fastest. Give them a wider starting gap if needed.

drills.title: Rats and Rabbits
drills.objective: React and accelerate.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Pair players on two parallel lines, each facing their own safety line. Call one team; they run to safety while partners pursue for a light tag. Reset.
drills.coaching: React to the call; leave room to decelerate.
drills.regression: Use a visual signal and walking.
drills.progression: Mix visual and verbal cues.
drills.questions: What helped you react to the call? How did you slow down at the end?
drills.notes: Call both teams equally. Leave a clear run-off beyond each safety line; switch partners regularly.

drills.title: Rob the Nest
drills.objective: Scan and change direction.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.equipment: 5 hoops or marked nests, 8 balls, cones
drills.instructions: Place balls at centre with teams at corner nests. One runner per team collects one ball each trip; then tag the next teammate. No stealing from hands.
drills.coaching: Look up at centre; carry securely.
drills.progression: Allow taking one unattended ball from another nest.
drills.questions: Which nest has the clearest route? Where will you look before picking up the ball?
drills.notes: One child runs per team; the rest wait behind their nest. Count balls at the end instead of encouraging children to wrestle for them.

drills.title: Animal Walks Relay
drills.objective: Develop coordination and balance.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Set short parallel lanes. Children explore bear crawls and other comfortable animal movements, then return walking. Keep bouts short.
drills.coaching: Move with control; stop if uncomfortable.
drills.progression: Combine two movement patterns.
drills.questions: Which movement is easiest to control? Can you keep the same balance when you change direction?
drills.notes: Let children choose a comfortable movement. This is coordination practice, not a race or fitness punishment.

drills.title: Mirror Movement
drills.objective: Track direction without crossing feet unnecessarily.
drills.safety: Use agreed light touch or tags only, not tackles. Keep the playing area and run-off clear.
drills.instructions: Partners face each other with a safe gap; leader shuffles and changes direction for 10–15 seconds. Follower mirrors without touching; swap.
drills.coaching: Stay balanced; watch torso and hips.
drills.progression: Add forward and backward movement.
drills.questions: What tells you your partner is about to change direction? How can you stay balanced?
drills.notes: Keep the partners facing one another and give each pair room. Change leader after a short bout.

drills.title: Balance Challenge
drills.objective: Develop single-leg control.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: In personal spaces, stand on one leg briefly, reach or receive a gentle pass, then switch. Keep movements comfortable.

drills.questions: What helps you stay steady? Can you catch without putting your other foot down?

drills.title: Passing Gauntlet
drills.objective: Pass accurately while moving.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.players: One runner and three feeders per lane; rotate roles.
drills.instructions: Place feeders at successive stations. Runners collect a pass from behind or level with the feeder, move just beyond them and return the ball sideways or backwards. Rotate feeders often.
drills.coaching: Keep eyes up; turn hands toward ball; avoid rushing.
drills.progression: Vary distance and timing of feeds.
drills.questions: When should the feeder release the ball? Can the runner catch without stopping?
drills.notes: Three separate balls are used. The runner moves past each feeder before returning the ball; keep the next runner back until the lane is clear. Feeders are stationary handling partners, not advancing teammates.

drills.title: Diamond Passing
drills.objective: Create useful support angles.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Start four players in a diamond; pass to a moving adjacent player and follow into the vacated position. Reset if spacing collapses.
drills.coaching: Call early; move as ball travels; maintain distance.
drills.progression: Add a roaming passive defender.
drills.questions: When can the passer follow? How much space should the next receiver leave?
drills.notes: The diamond is a non-directional catch-and-follow pattern with no attacking end. Pass only to a clear target. Use the continuous passing drill next to practise sideways and backward passes towards a fixed try line.

Slow down before corners rather than rushing the turn. This is a modified handling game without a fixed match attack direction. For directional rugby practice, require sideways or backward passes.

drills.title: Bench Ball
drills.objective: Move to receive in a target zone.
drills.safety: Use agreed light touch or tags only, not tackles. Keep the playing area and run-off clear.
drills.instructions: Teams pass to a teammate stationed in a marked end zone (no raised bench). Score and rotate target players. No contact.
drills.coaching: Move after passing; call and see the receiver.
drills.progression: Make target zone smaller.
drills.questions: Where can the target player move to receive? Can teammates create a better passing lane?
drills.notes: Use a ground-level end zone, never a bench or raised object. Rotate target players regularly. This is a modified handling game without a fixed match attack direction. For directional rugby practice, require sideways or backward passes.

drills.title: Partner Tag
drills.objective: Evade and track with control.
drills.safety: Keep the exercise non-contact. Allow room between groups and adapt the pace to the players.
drills.instructions: Pairs stay in their own small lane; one tries to escape a light tag for a short interval and roles swap.
drills.coaching: Eyes up; use short changes of direction; no grabbing.
drills.progression: Add a scoring gate.
drills.questions: What helped you avoid the tag? Can you track without grabbing or lunging?
drills.notes: Keep each pair inside its own lane and use short rounds. Stop a repetition if players enter adjacent lanes.

drills.title: 2 to Score · Multi-defender channel
drills.objective: Repeat draw-and-pass decisions.
drills.safety: Use agreed light touch or tags only, not tackles. Keep the playing area and run-off clear.
drills.instructions: Two attackers progress down a channel against defenders placed at intervals, each limited to lateral movement. Rotate frequently; touch only.
drills.coaching: Run toward space; keep receiver available; vary decisions.
drills.progression: Allow a defender to advance.
drills.questions: Can the carrier beat this defender without a pass? Is the support player still available at the next gate?
drills.notes: Defenders stay in their assigned lateral lanes. Rotate both attackers and defenders so everyone practises the choices.

drills.title: Cone Slalom · Curved Running
drills.objective: Change direction smoothly while carrying the ball in two hands.
drills.safety: Non-contact movement exercise. Leave sufficient space around equipment and other children; no live collisions. Adjust pace and spacing to ability.
drills.instructions: Set up cones in a straight line. Run around alternate sides of each cone, maintaining control before accelerating through the finish. Rotate frequently; leave room between runners.
drills.coaching: Look ahead, keep the ball secure, vary pace and use small controlled steps.
drills.regression: Walk through the pattern first; increase spacing.
drills.progression: After the final cone, add a touch defender or a passing option.
drills.questions: Where do you need to slow down? When is the lane clear enough to accelerate?
drills.notes: The curved route is a guide to the intended running line. Increase cone spacing for children who need more time to turn.
drills.provenance: Original illustrative coaching adaptation; not a reproduction of an official drill.

drills.title: Support Arc · Around an Obstacle
drills.objective: Move around congestion and arrive in a useful support position.
drills.safety: Non-contact movement exercise. Leave sufficient space around equipment and other children; no live collisions. Adjust pace and spacing to ability.
drills.equipment: Cones; optional ball; a marker for congestion
drills.instructions: Use cones or a marker to represent a stationary group. A support runner arcs around the outside, avoiding the occupied space. Coach the running line only, not contact or legal maul entry.
drills.coaching: Scan the space, avoid crossing in front of the carrier, communicate and maintain useful depth.
drills.regression: Walk the route without a ball.
drills.progression: Add a moving ball carrier or a passive touch defender; check age-grade offside requirements before using a maul scenario.
drills.questions: Where is the free route around the obstacle? Can you still receive a pass?
drills.notes: The contact-shaped marker represents occupied space only. Keep this a running-line exercise; do not teach side-entry to a live maul.

drills.title: U10 Breakdown · Tackle, Present, Support and Play
drills.objective: Recognise the sequence from tackle to a ball available to play, with one arriving support player each side.
drills.safety: Schematic coach-led demonstration. Contact technique must be taught by a qualified coach following current RFU age-grade rules. Rehearse the sequence without contact first.
drills.players: 3 attackers and 3 defenders; rotate carrier, tackler and support roles.
drills.instructions: Walk through A1's tackle, D1's release and the presentation. A2 arrives first; D2 then joins from the opposite side. Keep A3 and D3 out of the ruck. When the ball is available, A3 collects and passes to A2 after A2 has disengaged.
drills.coaching: Release and present without delay. The arriving players enter from their own side and remain on their feet. Once the ball is available, move it away rather than sending in another player.
drills.regression: Use a stationary ball and walk to the positions without binding or tackling.
drills.progression: Change which side arrives first in a no-contact walk-through; ask players to find the next receiver.
drills.questions: Why does A3 wait outside the ruck? When can A2 become a receiver again?
drills.notes: Shows a single tackle followed by one additional player from each team. The ruck is a positional diagram, not instruction in clearing out.

drills.title: U10 Shield Clearout · Defender Arrives First
drills.objective: Demonstrate the sequence of a tackle, ball presentation, defender arriving with a contact shield and attacking support arriving from their own side.
drills.safety: Schematic coach-led demonstration. Contact technique must be taught by a qualified coach following current RFU age-grade rules. Use a passive shield as a position marker; do not charge into a shield holder or teach a clearout from the animation.
drills.players: 3 attackers and 3 defenders; D2 holds the passive shield.
drills.equipment: Rugby ball, cones and a suitable contact shield.
drills.instructions: Start with D1 tracking A1 and A2 supporting. After the simulated tackle and presentation, D2 marks the defending arrival with the shield; A2 takes the attacking-side position. A3 plays the ball away and D2 hands the shield to D3 for the next turn.
drills.coaching: Ask A2 to approach from behind the ball and stay balanced. The shield is a marker for the defender's position, not a target to charge into. A3 waits to play the ball away.
drills.regression: Replace the shield with a cone and walk through the arrival order.
drills.progression: Swap the order of the arrivals without physical contact. Any shield-contact progression belongs to the qualified club coach.
drills.questions: Has a ruck formed when only D2 is standing over the ball? Who should play it away?
drills.notes: Although the title uses 'clearout', this resource teaches arrival order and position. It does not instruct children to drive into a shield holder at a breakdown.

drills.title: U10 · Scrum
drills.objective: Understand the roles, feed and exit of an uncontested U10 scrum.
drills.safety: Use an unbound walk-through. Any engagement or contact must be led by a qualified scrum coach under the relevant age-grade rules.
drills.players: Three forwards per side, A1 and D10 as scrum-halves, A2 as first receiver.
drills.instructions: Mark the scrum. Position A3–A5 and D1–D3 as the two packs without binding. A1 feeds and later collects; A2 waits in a receiving position. D10 stays behind the defending scrum. Discuss where other backs would stand.
drills.coaching: The U10 scrum is uncontested: no pushing, only the feeding hooker strikes, and the feeding scrum-half passes away. Follow the referee's instructions.
drills.regression: Use six cones to represent the forwards and one child to move the ball through the positions.
drills.progression: Swap feeding and defending roles in the unbound walk-through.
drills.questions: Who is allowed to strike for the ball? What must the feeding scrum-half do after collecting?
drills.notes: A1 both feeds and collects in the animation. A2 receives the pass. The 2026–27 U10 summary describes the three-player, no-push scrum; check the current RFU appendix before practice.

drills.title: U10 · Maul
drills.objective: Recognise when an upright hold becomes a maul and how the ball leaves it.
drills.safety: Walk through positions only. No holding, pulling, collapsing or driving in this demonstration; qualified supervision is required for contact practice.
drills.players: A1 carrier, A3 support, D1 opponent and A2 receiver.
drills.instructions: Position A1 and D1 without making contact. Add A3 to explain how a maul forms. Show the ball moving to A3, then being passed to A2. Stop the walk-through before adding any force.
drills.coaching: A held carrier alone is not a formed maul. Keep players on their feet; observe U10 participation limits and move the ball away promptly.
drills.regression: Represent the three involved roles with cones and move the ball by hand.
drills.progression: Change which teammate is the receiver, without adding participants to the maul.
drills.questions: At which step does the maul form? Where does A2 wait to receive?
drills.notes: The diagram shows two blue players and one orange player in the maul. It does not simulate forward momentum or a legal drive.

drills.title: U14 · Lineout · throw and catch
drills.objective: Recognise the thrower, catcher, two lines and first receiver at an uncontested lineout.
drills.safety: Uncontested and unlifted practice only. Keep a clear landing area and follow the current U14 rules before any progression.
drills.players: A1 throws, A3 catches, A2 receives; A4–A5 and D1–D3 illustrate the two lines.
drills.instructions: Mark touch and the lineout corridor. Walk to the positions, have A1 throw to A3 without a contest, then let A3 settle on their feet before passing to A2.
drills.coaching: Give the thrower a clear target; catch with control and pass only when balanced. Players not participating remain at the required offside distance.
drills.regression: Short throw to a stationary catcher, with no opposition line.
drills.progression: Change the named catcher and the direction of the next pass while keeping the throw uncontested.
drills.questions: Who catches? Where should the receiver wait? What changes if the throw is inaccurate?
drills.notes: This is an U14 positioning example, not a full-match lineout or a lifting lesson. Check the applicable age-grade conditions.

drills.title: U10 · Offload to support
drills.objective: Recognise a safe backward pass to support before a carrier goes to ground.
drills.safety: No opponent contact is shown or needed. Any later contact practice requires a qualified coach.
drills.players: A1 carrier and A2 support; no opponent in the diagram.
drills.instructions: Start with two players standing apart. Ask A2 to offer a target from behind A1. A1 passes before any simulated grounding. Repeat from the other side; only add passive touch pressure once the pass is reliable.
drills.coaching: Look before passing. Support calls early and stays behind the carrier. If the pass is not available, do not force it.
drills.regression: Stationary two-handed pass to a nearby support player.
drills.progression: Add a touch defender to give A1 a carry-or-pass decision.
drills.questions: Where is A2 relative to the ball? What happens if A2 arrives too late?
drills.notes: This shows just the offload pass. It does not teach a pass from the ground or contact technique.

drills.title: U10 · Free pass restart
drills.objective: Understand the stationary free pass and when players may move in U10.
drills.safety: No charging onto the pass or rushing an unready receiver. Walk through the restart initially.
drills.players: A1 passer and A2 receiver; add opponents for a supervised walk-through.
drills.instructions: Place the ball at the referee's restart mark. A2 stands behind A1. Check the defenders have retired the required distance, then A1 passes on the referee's signal. Players move only after the pass.
drills.coaching: Two hands, a backward pass, no run-up. Use the referee's mark, not the location of the previous ball by default.
drills.regression: Two stationary players and cones to show the retreat line.
drills.progression: Add defenders behind the marked line, then continue a touch game after the pass.
drills.questions: When may A2 start running? Where do the defenders wait?
drills.notes: The 2026–27 U10 summary specifies a 7 m retreat and a restart 5 m in from touch where applicable. The two-player diagram does not draw the defending line.

drills.safety: No charging defenders. Only practise restart kicks permitted for the age group by the current rules.

drills.coaching: The ball must be visibly kicked for a tap. A2 remains available behind the taker. Do not assume the same choices apply to a free kick and a penalty.
drills.regression: Walk through the positions and discuss the tap before using the ball.
drills.progression: Add a passive defending line at the correct retreat distance once the coach has checked the law.
drills.questions: What makes the tap visible? Where can A2 stand?

drills.objective: Recognise a try as grounding the ball in the opponents' in-goal area.
drills.safety: No diving, chasing into the boundary, or contested grounding. Use a suitable surface and leave space beyond the line.
drills.players: A1 carrier and A2 observing or supporting.

drills.instructions: Set the ball on a tee at an agreed mark. Give the kicker an unobstructed approach. Aim towards the target; wait until the area is clear before retrieving the ball.

drills.title: U10 · Read the defender — tackle or offload
drills.objective: Recognise when to carry into space, keep possession through contact or pass to a teammate in support. Compare demonstrated and alternative actions.
drills.safety: Schematic coach-led demonstration. Contact technique must be taught by a qualified coach following current RFU age-grade rules. Use a passive shield as a position marker; do not charge into a shield holder or teach a clearout from the animation.
drills.players: 3 attackers, 3 defenders; D2 marks the defending arrival with a passive shield.

drills.coaching: Scan before contact. If a safe pass is not available, do not force it. Release and present immediately after grounding; support arrives from its own side and stays on its feet. Keep other players clear.
drills.regression: Show the alternatives without contact, using a cone instead of a shield.
drills.progression: Vary the support runner's starting position and let the carrier choose during touch practice.
drills.questions: Where is the space? Is support available for a safe backwards offload? When should the carrier secure the ball instead?

drills.title: U10 · Two defenders, one carrier — double tackle and release
drills.objective: Recognise defensive communication and immediate release responsibilities for both tacklers.
drills.players: 1 carrier, 2 defenders, supporting players as observers.

drills.regression: Walk the two defensive approach routes with the carrier stopping at a cone.
drills.progression: Swap the starting sides and ask defenders to communicate who tracks first; no live contact needed.
drills.questions: Who must release? Where should the other defenders stand?
drills.notes: This ends at release rather than a ruck. The current U10 contact and participation rules need club review before practising double tackles.

drills.title: U10 · Two-phase attack — recycle and go again
drills.objective: Connect two phases and reorganise behind the ball.

drills.questions: Where does A2 go after the first phase? Who supports the second carrier?
drills.notes: The first ruck and second tackle are separate events. A3 passes away before receiving again in open play; no pick-and-go from the formed U10 ruck is implied.
